structural_findings.finding: The existing backend audit scans JSON recursively, but the repository's canonical audit report still records the full recursive inventory as pending.
structural_findings.action: Keep the audit report machine-generated and promote recursive JSON/schema/ID/route checks into the release gate.

structural_findings.finding: The repository already has a generic node resolver and long-form infrastructure, but the long-form dossier layer is not yet populated for every important record.
structural_findings.action: Measure rendered depth and prioritize high-connectivity shallow records before creating more labels.

structural_findings.finding: Religious foundation data has multiple layers and an explicit validator, but the workflow still identifies enriched foundation synchronization as unfinished work.
structural_findings.action: Treat canonical ownership and enrichment synchronization as a release blocker for that layer.

structural_findings.finding: 195 country identities exist, but the missing-data registry explicitly reports only one country with validated sourced-core enrichment.
structural_findings.action: Expand country evidence in batches using dated observations, sources and explicit missing states rather than treating overlay presence as research depth.

structural_findings.finding: Security/extremism datasets are registered and addressable, but integration into the canonical graph remains an explicit workflow task.
structural_findings.action: Promote documented organizations and successor/affiliate relationships into canonical graph records without conflating classifications.

structural_findings.finding: The relationship-first design requires endpoint resolution, while the existing audit intentionally permits research-only endpoints.
structural_findings.action: Generate a ranked orphan queue and promote the most connected unresolved IDs first.

structural_findings.finding: The new Root/Spirit/Door/Matter navigation is now explicit, while the older 33-level tree remains a deeper architecture.
structural_findings.action: Keep both: the spine is the primary temporal navigation; the 33-level tree is the detailed vertical scaffold. Do not replace one with the other.

structural_findings.finding: The repository manifest describes many canonical datasets that the Repository page does not yet expose individually.
structural_findings.action: Continue widening discovery so backend-only research layers are searchable without making the root visually noisy.

structural_findings.finding: The project contains large Edda texts and complete scripture-layer infrastructure, but text metadata, passages and interpretation need consistent cross-links.
structural_findings.action: Treat text as a first-class source/corpus layer with stable locators and links into people, places, events and concepts.

structural_findings.finding: The new spine defines future/present/past, but individual records do not yet consistently carry temporal status fields.
structural_findings.action: Add valid_from, valid_to, observed_at, published_at, supersedes and relationship-state fields where applicable.

architecture_decision: Root/Spine -> Spirit/Future -> Door/Present -> Matter/Past is the primary navigation model. Existing 33-level architecture, graph, evidence and domain datasets remain subordinate/orthogonal structures rather than being deleted or forced into one taxonomy.
known_good_principles: relationships are not proof of causation
project canon remains distinct from empirical evidence
counts do not equal substantive research
do not create duplicate IDs solely for navigation
a graph edge is not a substitute for a dossier
next_release_gate: All critical structural validators pass; recursive audit is current; high-connectivity route depth has been measured; canonical religious and graph layers are synchronized; CI confirms the result.
